_README: Batch 19 facts (D-insure + D-entry) — reconciled 2026-07-24 from deepseek+grok, rulings in disputes-batch19.md. ENTIRELY YMYL. Merge into thailandforamericans/facts.json.
_STATUS_RULING: deepseek marked 24 of 40 facts 'verified' against an explicit instruction to default to verify_recommended. Auditing the source URLs: only 2 of those 24 cite an official government source. The other 22 cite visa agencies (shathailand.com, thailandelite.net), hospital marketing pages, an insurer's own claims page, and a booking site. Those are DOWNGRADED to verify_recommended here. Where I independently confirmed a fact against a Thai embassy or .go.th immigration source, it is marked verified with THAT source, not the model's.

immigration_mechanics._note: Independently web-verified against Royal Thai Embassy and Thai immigration sources. Both panel members agreed on every number here before verification.

overstay_fine.value: 500 baht per day, capped at 20,000 baht — the cap is reached at 40 days and the fine stops accumulating after that
overstay_fine.notes: Both panel members agreed; confirmed against Royal Thai Embassy Washington DC. Also confirmed at bucharest.thaiembassy.org and samutprakanimmigration.go.th.

overstay_short_waiver.value: For an overstay of a few hours caused by a flight delay or schedule change, the fine is usually waived when explained to the immigration officer at departure
overstay_short_waiver.notes: Stated directly by the embassy. Neither panel member surfaced this and it is the most reassuring fact in the section.

overstay_ban_voluntary.value: Surrendering voluntarily: under 90 days is a fine with no re-entry ban; over 90 days brings a 1-year ban; over 1 year a 3-year ban; over 3 years a 5-year ban; over 5 years a 10-year ban
overstay_ban_voluntary.notes: Thai immigration .go.th source confirms the 90-day and 1-year thresholds. Both panel members gave the same ladder.

overstay_caught_vs_surrender.value: Being caught rather than surrendering carries substantially harsher consequences including detention and a longer ban; the cash fine is the same either way
overstay_caught_vs_surrender.notes: Both agree on the structure. Exact ban lengths when caught differ across sources, so only the direction is stated.

where_fine_is_paid.value: At the immigration counter on departure, at an airport or land border; officers calculate the days, collect the fine and issue a receipt
where_fine_is_paid.notes: Embassy also notes that travellers unable to pay may be held until funds are raised.

extension_length.notes: Both panel members agreed; grok cited the US Embassy in Thailand.

extension_where.value: At a Thai Immigration Bureau office

extension_documents.value: TM7 application form, passport, a passport photo, and copies; proof of address may be requested
extension_documents.notes: Both agree on the core list. DS added detail from a visa agency page — downgraded.

extension_processing.value: Usually same day if filed early in the day

extension_how_many.value: Commonly once per entry for a visa exemption or tourist visa; anything beyond that is discretionary

tdac.value: The Thailand Digital Arrival Card replaced the paper TM6 in May 2025. It is mandatory, free, filed online before arrival
tdac.notes: Both agree. Official Thai immigration domain. DS says within 3 days of arrival — filing window is CHANGE-PRONE, do not state a precise window without re-checking.

onward_ticket_enforcement.value: Checked primarily by airlines at check-in rather than by immigration on arrival
onward_ticket_enforcement.notes: Both agree. Practically important: the airline is the party that turns people away.

proof_of_funds.value: A funds requirement exists in the regulations — commonly cited as 20,000 baht per person or 40,000 per family — but it is not routinely checked in practice
proof_of_funds.notes: DS cited a Thai embassy page for the amounts. Enforcement reality is the unsourced half; stated as the gap it is.

entry_stamp_check.value: Verify the 'admitted until' date written on the entry stamp before leaving the immigration desk
entry_stamp_check.notes: Both agree. The date on the stamp governs, not the traveller's assumption about the exemption length.

border_run_status.value: Leaving and re-entering produces a new entry stamp, but repeated back-to-back entries attract additional scrutiny and are not guaranteed
border_run_status.notes: Both agree. HIGHLY CHANGE-PRONE — policy has tightened repeatedly.

medical_mechanics._note: Category-level only. Never adjudicate a specific policy, never name an insurer as good or bad.

emergency_number.value: 1669 for medical emergencies nationwide; 1155 for the Tourist Police, which is English-speaking
emergency_number.notes: Both gave 1669. DS added 1155 Tourist Police, which is the more useful number for a visitor with a language barrier.

direct_billing_vs_reimbursement.value: Private Thai hospitals commonly require payment or a guarantee of payment before treating a foreign patient. Direct billing happens where the insurer issues a guarantee to that hospital; otherwise the patient pays and claims back afterwards
direct_billing_vs_reimbursement.notes: Both agree. THE MOST PRACTICALLY IMPORTANT MECHANIC IN THE BATCH — it decides whether a traveller needs funds available at the moment of the emergency.

guarantee_of_payment.value: A guarantee of payment is the document an insurer issues to a hospital to enable direct billing; obtaining one means contacting the insurer's assistance line rather than the hospital
guarantee_of_payment.notes: DS supplied the mechanism; GK described the same thing less specifically.

evacuation_vs_repatriation.value: Evacuation moves a patient to the nearest facility able to treat them. Repatriation returns them to their home country. They are separate coverages and a policy may include one without the other
evacuation_vs_repatriation.notes: Both agree. Commonly conflated by travellers.

interruption_vs_cancellation.value: Cancellation applies before departure; interruption applies once the trip has started. Interruption is the one that speaks to problems encountered abroad

claim_process.value: Notify the insurer's assistance line as early as possible, ideally before treatment; obtain itemised bills and medical reports from the hospital; submit for reimbursement where direct billing was not arranged

documentation.value: Itemised receipts, the doctor's report and proof of payment are what Thai hospitals issue and what insurers typically require

common_exclusions.value: Pre-existing conditions without a waiver, adventure activities without a rider, incidents involving alcohol or illegal acts, and routine or non-emergency care
common_exclusions.notes: Both agree. CATEGORY LEVEL — no insurer named.

adventure_exclusions.value: Motorbike riding, scuba diving, zip-lining and rock climbing are commonly excluded or require a rider
adventure_exclusions.notes: Both agree. Connects to the existing scooter article without repeating it.

pre_existing_conditions.value: Commonly excluded unless a waiver is purchased, typically requiring the condition to have been stable for a defined period
pre_existing_conditions.notes: Both agree on the shape; the stability period varies by policy and is not stated here.

payment_upfront.value: Private hospitals typically require payment or a guarantee before non-emergency treatment

public_vs_private.value: Private hospitals cost more and generally offer English-speaking staff and shorter waits; public hospitals cost less with longer waits and more variable English

pharmacy_scope.value: Thai pharmacies dispense many medications over the counter that would require a prescription in the United States
pharmacy_scope.notes: Both agree. Deliberately NOT listing which drugs — that would be medical advice.

consultation_cost.notes: VOLATILE. GK gave 1,000-5,000 baht for a private outpatient consultation; single-source and price-like, so not frozen into prose.

island_medical._note: The sharpest sub-topic — the corpus has nothing on it.

facilities_by_island.value: Koh Samui and Phuket have full private hospitals. Koh Phangan, Koh Tao, Koh Lanta and Koh Chang have clinics or basic facilities rather than full hospitals
facilities_by_island.notes: Both agree on the split. DS sourced it to hospital marketing pages — downgraded, but the substance is corroborated by both.

hyperbaric_chambers.value: Koh Tao has hyperbaric chamber facilities, which matters because it is one of the world's busiest dive-training destinations. Koh Phangan and Phuket also have chambers
hyperbaric_chambers.notes: Both agree Koh Tao has one. DS adds Phangan and Phuket, and states Koh Samui does not — that last claim is single-source and is NOT written into prose.

transfer_to_bangkok.value: By boat plus ambulance, or by air ambulance where the island has an airstrip and the case warrants it

who_arranges.value: The insurer's assistance line coordinates evacuation with local providers; it is not arranged by the patient or typically by the treating clinic
who_arranges.notes: Both agree. Practically important: the number to call is the insurer's, not an ambulance service.

evacuation_cost.value: Costs run into the tens of thousands of US dollars, with dedicated air ambulance at the higher end
evacuation_cost.notes: RULED. DS gave $10,000-50,000+; GK gave 'tens to hundreds of thousands'. They overlap at the lower bound only, so the shared floor is stated as an order of magnitude rather than either range.

timing.notes: UNSOURCED. GK said 'hours to same day' unsourced; DS gave a range from a commercial page. Not written into prose.

_open_questions._note: Carried from both panel members plus the verification pass.
items: Exact TDAC filing window — DS says within 3 days of arrival, unconfirmed against the official site and highly change-prone
Ban lengths when caught rather than surrendering — sources disagree
Whether Koh Samui has a hyperbaric chamber — single-source negative claim, not published
Island-to-Bangkok medical transfer timing — no reliable figure
Pre-existing condition waiver stability periods — vary by policy, not generalisable
Typical private consultation cost — single-source and volatile
